market_view: Stocks go into Monday fragile: the S&P 500 bounced only 0.32% to 7,376.86 on Nov 6 after Thursday's -4.36% AI/chip rout, with VIX still 25.5 and the 10-year at 4.86% (JournalArta, Nov 6), and Nasdaq futures are weaker Sunday night after reports that Microsoft is winding down its AI-compute rental deal with Oracle (ORCL -4% Friday; TokenPost, Nov 8) on top of the post-midterm hit to data-center power names (CEG -9% in two sessions; TIKR, Nov 6). The only scheduled catalysts are Monday earnings (CEG, KKR, FERG, NRG before the open; TTWO after the close; TheStreet, Nov 8), which will already be priced into the open we would buy, so I add nothing tonight; no operator update asked for anything I had to ignore.
lessons: I'm still losing to the market and to both baselines: alpha -1.14% per trade over 82 trades (95% range -2.09% to -0.19%, p_beats_fly 0.024) versus -0.08% for the Fruit Fly and -0.43% for Momentum, and my moonshots (n=40, 15% win) and catalysts (n=43, 48.8% stopped) both lose. Tonight's only catalysts are Monday pre-market earnings (CEG, KKR, NRG), and the lab shows first-session buys lose 1.6% on average and +2% gap opens lose 5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch), so I submit no moonshots or catalysts rather than buy a gapped open.

My non-AI compounders made +$0.96 on Nov 6 and all three sit above entry (BLK +3.6%, LLY +3.6%, ABBV +0.1%) while AI-linked names keep breaking (my GOOGL -17.7% and NVDA -11.6% stops, ORCL -4% Friday on the Microsoft compute wind-down); compounder n=5 is a hunch, but it's the one place I'm not bleeding, so I keep it diversified and add no AI-capex or data-center-power name.

Friday's ranges show my LLY stop is still too tight: LLY traded $1,333-$1,377 (3.2%) on Nov 6, so 1.5x range is ~4.9%, and the $1,295 stop is only 4.4% under the $1,354 close; I'm moving it to $1,285 (5.1%). ChatGPT's compounder book (+1.89%, n=5) shows patience with empty slots costs nothing, so I keep my two free slots empty until the tape calms (VIX 25.5) instead of buying into a weak Nasdaq open.

review.reason: BlackRock rose 0.7% to $1,178.87 on Nov 6 (range $1,155.52-$1,195.19) with no company-specific negative news, so the Q3 inflection thesis ($205B net inflows, adj. EPS $15.93) is intact; the $1,120 stop sits ~5% below the close, outside 1.5x its daily range.

Lilly's Oct 29 beat and raise (Q3 revenue +39% to $24.4B, 2026 revenue guide lifted to $91-92B; TIKR, Nov 5) still drives the thesis and Friday's -0.8% to $1,354 was noise, but the $1,295 stop sat inside 1.5x Friday's 3.2% range, so I lower it to $1,285 (~5.1% below the close).

AbbVie gained 1.1% to $291.31 on Nov 6 and its raised 2026 EPS guide of $13.95-13.99 plus the Nxera licensing deal (MarketBeat, Nov 4) keep the beat-and-raise thesis intact; the $272 stop (~6.6% below) stays outside normal noise.
